The Harionago Selvedge is a 14oz Japanese selvedge denim woven at low tension and left unsinged, resulting in a pronounced hairy surface texture. Made from 100% cotton and rope-dyed in indigo, the fabric embraces raw, expressive character and visible irregularity.
The denim draws its inspiration from the Japanese yōkai Harionago , a supernatural figure whose name translates to “Barbed-Hair Woman.” In Japanese folklore, Harionago is depicted as a beautiful but dangerous spirit who uses her long, thorn-like hair to ensnare and kill her victims. Her hair is often described as sharp, tangled, and inescapable; a visual metaphor echoed in the denim’s untamed, bristled surface.
This mythological reference is translated directly into material form. The unsinged fibers and rough texture mirror the creature’s wild hair, while custom artwork by Canadian artist Jacqui Oakley reinforces the narrative connection between folklore and fabric.

The Citrus Kasuri Weft Selvedge is a 14oz Japanese selvedge denim distinguished by its complex weft dyeing technique. Beneath the indigo surface lies a vibrant interior created using traditional Kasuri methods.
Rather than inserting solid-colored weft yarns, Kasuri dyeing involves binding and selectively dyeing sections of yarn before weaving. This results in alternating yellow and green segments along the same yarn, producing organic, patterned coloration rather than uniform stripes.
As the denim wears and abrasions develop, the citrus-toned weft gradually reveals itself through the indigo surface. Due to the labor-intensive nature of Kasuri dyeing, this fabric is used sparingly, making it both expressive and rare.

What might seem like a simple piece from us rarely is. This garment-dyed Quilted Hunting Jacket took on a couple forms and went through quite a few rounds of sampling before we found where we wanted it to be. The initial idea spawned from the old Czech military liners, as well as our appreciation for quilted jackets from more traditional heritage brands. Initial rounds were too shiny, too bright, too expensive, but most importantly didn't feel like us. We put it on ice until we found another Korean War-era quilted jacket that was beautifully washed out, the fabric was a bit irregular, the stitching was non-traditional, and all of those things inspired us to take the quilted jacket in a different direction.
We had to develop a fabric that had some irregularity but would also take dyes and washes in a way that we could work with. We also had to tackle some construction hurdles in order to ensure we could quilt both sides, and thus change the construction to work with that. A couple dye and wash tests later we were almost there.

p-wythenewyork-9048524193923.d:
All of our corduroy from the comes from one of our favorite mills in Italy which specializes in weaving only corduroys and velvets. They've been weaving corduroy since the late 1800s, and still have a stream running through the mill which they use to wash and clean the cotton.
An exclusive fabric to Wythe, the donegal cords came about when we were looking for a corduroy to compliment our donegal tweed. We approached this historic corduroy mill with some of our inspiration, and we worked together to go through their archive to come up with the answer. Throughout the years, they had come up with their own printing process to achieve a donegal effect in their signature super-soft corduroy. This effect is unique to this mill and there are many steps involved in the process to create this beautiful fabric.
The Donegal Cord Barn Jacket should be a familiar silhouette to you by now. Our coverall jacket-inspired body felt like a great place for our Donegal Corduroy, especially with our love of vintage French corduroy work jackets. This might be the quintessential Fall jacket for easy layering.

Bandanas have been around in many forms since humans have first needed a go to fabric for anything and everything. Bandanas turned up as headscarves, dust masks, neck guards, wrist splints, belts, trail markers, pot holders, knapsacks, napkins, truly anything and everything. Designs began to change form in the early 1900s to the outer border and inside border, which is what we generally recognize now as a bandana pattern. The Wythe designs are based on "Elephant Brand" bandanas from the 1930's and 40's, referencing traditional designs and making them new. The Fast Colour Steer is our nod to the Elephants that adorned this era of bandanas.
We went to a small atelier in Japan that specializes in Indigo Discharge printing, which is very old and intricate process in which a fabric is dyed completely with indigo then the pattern or design is literally "removed" by a discharge printing process similar to a bleach. This leaves the design in the natural colour of the cotton and ensures that the design is clean on both sides of the bandana.
